meta.description: Query and download from NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and EMBL-EBI's BioStudies/ArrayExpress mirror. Use when finding expression datasets, navigating SuperSeries vs SubSeries, choosing between series-matrix (submitter-normalized) and raw supplementary files, downloading via GEOparse (Python) or GEOquery (R/Bioconductor), linking GEO to SRA for raw reads, or distinguishing GSE/GSM/GPL/GDS record types. Encodes the SuperSeries trap, the series-matrix normalization-trust caveat, GEOmetadb deprecation, ArrayExpress migration to BioStudies, and processed-vs-raw decision matrix.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results/p-values in any output. The examples/geo_from_pubmed.py PMID mislabel (Input 4) is an upstream documentation bug -- the code queries live NCBI data honestly and reports whatever it finds (0 real links); it never invents a result.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic/prescriptive medical conclusions in any output; this is a database-access skill with no clinical framing.

methodological_ground.detail: No output committed a methodological fallacy. Input 7 (adversarial 'skip the SuperSeries check, mix everything for one PCA') correctly refused to silently comply, citing the Skill's own documented mixed-platform/mixed-batch failure mode instead of proceeding naively.

code_usability.detail: All code ran (no syntax errors, no missing dependencies, no infinite loops). Three separate runtime defects were found in examples/ (ValueError in search_geo.py's detect_super_series, TypeError in geo_to_sra.py's Entrez fallback, and a wrong hardcoded PMID in geo_from_pubmed.py) but none meet M4's specific trigger list (syntax error / infinite loop / missing dependency); each is scored instead under Reliability, Layer 1/2, and P1 recommendations. Consistent with this folder's prior audits (e.g. bio-entrez-fetch, bio-entrez-link) treating comparable example-script API-mismatch bugs as scoring findings, not a code-usability veto.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness is strong (search, SuperSeries detection, series-matrix parsing, decision matrix, GEOparse/GEOquery, GEO->SRA, PubMed->GEO, GEOmetadb/ArrayExpress status all covered). Correctness is held down by all 3 examples/ scripts carrying a live-confirmed runtime bug (detect_super_series ValueError, geo_to_sra TypeError, wrong PMID) even though SKILL.md's own inline code patterns are largely correct.

reliability.note: Near-zero error handling in examples/ (no try/except around the Entrez/gzip/urllib calls that are documented to fail); errors surface as raw Python tracebacks (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError), not domain-specific messages. Re-running is safe (no destructive side effects) but nothing helps a user recover from the documented failure points.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is a reasonable 373 lines with usage-guide.md and examples/ split out; ESearch->ESummary/ELink chains are minimal and linear, no redundant round-trips observed in execution.

agent_usability.note: Code patterns are clearly labeled (Goal/Approach headers) and the SuperSeries warning is repeated consistently. One real ambiguity found: Entrez's db='gds' endpoint (indexes GSE/GSM/GPL/GDS together) is never disambiguated from 'GDS' the frozen curated-record type in the very next taxonomy table -- confusing on a literal read.

human_usability.note: Discoverability is good (natural trigger phrasing). Forgiveness is weak: a literal reading of the usage-guide's own 'dump every unique value of !Sample_data_processing' prompt crashes with KeyError on a real series (GSE470) that has zero such lines -- confirmed live in Input 3.

security.note: No hardcoded credentials (Entrez.email/api_key are placeholders); no sensitive-data retention. Accession/PMID strings are interpolated into URLs/E-utilities queries without explicit sanitization, though all tested values are simple alphanumeric accessions.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md / usage-guide.md / examples/ separation. No bundled test cases or expected-output fixtures, so the 3 live example-script bugs found here were not caught by anything shipped with the Skill.

agent_specific.note: Strong trigger description, correct progressive disclosure (373-line SKILL.md, examples/ split out), well-documented Related Skills hand-offs (sra-data, entrez-link, entrez-search), and genuinely strong escape-hatch guidance (the repeated SuperSeries warning functioned exactly as intended in Input 7).

recommendations.title: examples/geo_from_pubmed.py hardcodes the wrong PMID
recommendations.problem: PMID '32228226' is labeled 'Blanco-Melo et al. 2020 Cell (COVID-19 transcriptional response)' but is a live-confirmed different paper (Emerg Microbes Infect) with zero linked GDS records, so the example silently produces an empty, unhelpful result.
recommendations.root_cause: Wrong PMID was hardcoded when the example was written; never validated against a live elink call.
recommendations.fix: Replace PMID '32228226' with '32416070' (live-confirmed to link to GSE147507), and align the comment with examples/geo_to_sra.py, which already hardcodes GSE147507 for 'the same paper' -- the two examples are currently internally inconsistent about which PMID matches which GSE.

recommendations.title: examples/search_geo.py's detect_super_series() crashes with ValueError on every call
recommendations.problem: gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data), mode='rt') raises ValueError: Invalid mode: 'rt' -- GzipFile has no text mode. This breaks the shipped example on its very first live FTP round-trip, even though SKILL.md's own inline check_super_or_sub_series() (save to disk, then gzip.open(path, 'rt')) works correctly and was used successfully in this audit's Inputs 1 and 5.
recommendations.root_cause: The examples/ copy restructured the download to stay in-memory via BytesIO but kept the disk-based gzip.open() call signature, which GzipFile does not support in text mode.
recommendations.fix: Either call gzip.open() via io.TextIOWrapper(gzip.GzipFile(fileobj=..., mode='rb'), encoding='utf-8'), or simply reuse SKILL.md's own save-to-disk pattern that already works.

recommendations.title: examples/geo_to_sra.py's Entrez fallback raises TypeError on current Biopython
recommendations.problem: gse_to_srr_entrez()'s Entrez.efetch(db='sra', ..., retmode='text').read() returns bytes on the installed Biopython 1.88, but the code calls text.strip().split('\n') directly, raising TypeError: a bytes-like object is required, not 'str'. Not separately re-run in this audit (already confirmed by this folder's tooling pass 2026-09-17), listed here as an open, unfixed defect a fixer should still address.
recommendations.root_cause: Entrez.efetch's retmode='text' does not text-wrap this particular SRA content type on the current Biopython version; the code assumes it does.
recommendations.fix: Decode the handle content before string operations, e.g. text = h.read(); text = text.decode() if isinstance(text, bytes) else text.

recommendations.title: SKILL.md's own SuperSeries worked example no longer demonstrates a SuperSeries
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's inline docstring shows check_super_or_sub_series('GSE122288') returning {'super_of': ['GSExxxxx', 'GSEyyyyy'], 'sub_of': None}, but running the exact code against the real, live accession returns {'super_of': [], 'sub_of': None} -- GSE122288 is a standalone Series, not a SuperSeries.
recommendations.root_cause: The docstring's return value is an illustrative placeholder that was never validated against live data for this specific accession, and is presented as if it were the call's real output.
recommendations.fix: Either label the shown return value explicitly as illustrative/placeholder, or replace GSE122288 with a real, currently-still-a-SuperSeries accession so a user who runs the snippet verbatim sees a populated super_of list.

recommendations.title: No documented way to determine Affymetrix vs RNA-seq platform technology
recommendations.problem: The processed-vs-raw decision matrix repeatedly asks 'is this Affymetrix or RNA-seq' but no code pattern anywhere in SKILL.md, usage-guide.md, or examples/ shows how to determine platform technology from a GSE/GPL accession.
recommendations.root_cause: The decision matrix assumes the user already knows the platform technology rather than showing how to derive it from the GDS/GPL record.
recommendations.fix: Add a short code snippet resolving platform technology from the GDS record's title/technology fields or a GPL esummary call, ahead of the decision matrix.

recommendations.title: Series-matrix section doesn't warn that !Sample_data_processing can be entirely absent
recommendations.problem: The usage-guide's 'Submitter-data-processing audit' prompt, taken literally with bracket access, raises KeyError on a real series (GSE470) that has zero !Sample_data_processing lines. SKILL.md's own parse function uses the safe .get(key, []) form but nothing in the prose states the field can be fully absent, only that its content 'varies'.
recommendations.root_cause: The Series matrix section documents content variability but not field-absence as a distinct case.
recommendations.fix: Add one sentence: '!Sample_data_processing may be entirely absent on some series (e.g., older records) -- always use metadata.get(key, []) rather than direct key access.'

recommendations.title: 'GDS' is overloaded between the Entrez db name and the GDS record type
recommendations.problem: db='gds' is the Entrez endpoint indexing all four record types (GSE/GSM/GPL/GDS), but the GEO record taxonomy table immediately below uses 'GDS' to mean specifically the frozen curated-DataSet type. SKILL.md never disambiguates the two uses sitting right next to each other.
recommendations.root_cause: Terminology overlap between NCBI's own naming (db='gds') and the GEO record-type prefix (GDS) was not called out.
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line note: "Entrez's db='gds' indexes all four record types despite the name; don't confuse it with the GDS record type specifically."
